evidence_policy: Read-only primary-source research. Every revision, license and gate below was retrieved from the cited upstream source on retrieved_at. Nothing in this manifest asserts that any model was deployed, benchmarked or qualified on hardware; H100 fit states distinguish documented upstream support from untested expectation.

discovery.method: Read-only inspection on 2026-09-02 using the operator-provided acceptance kubeconfig, context k8s-inference-h100. Only get and list verbs were used. No object was created, patched or deleted, and no secret value was read; secrets were enumerated by name and type only.

observations: Two GPU nodes are Ready, each advertising eight allocatable GPUs of class nvidia-h100-sxm5-80gb in pool h100-reserved-8x, labelled capacity source capacity-block and capacity type regular. One general-purpose CPU node is also present.

Sixteen H100s are present in total and exactly one is currently consumed, by a single running Qwen inference pod in the fs2-models namespace. Fifteen GPUs are therefore free for this workload, subject to the shared-cluster policy of preserving other tenants.

The installed NVIDIA driver is 580.159.04. This satisfies the RFdiffusion microservice minimum of 580, so that lane is driver-ready. It does not satisfy the Boltz-2 microservice, which documents a minimum of 590.44.01 with CUDA 13.1, so any Boltz-2 microservice lane would require a driver upgrade to the shared cluster and must not be assumed available.

Two 128Gi ReadWriteMany model cache volumes already exist in the fs2-models namespace, for the Cosmos and Qwen lanes, on the shared filesystem storage class csi-mounted-fs-path-sc. The shared-cache pattern is therefore already established and this workload should extend it rather than invent a new one.
GPU nodes expose roughly 277 GiB of allocatable ephemeral storage, which is the node root disk. There is no large local NVMe scratch device on these nodes.

The three existing model deployments pull digest-pinned images from the in-project registry at cr.eu-north1.nebius.cloud and declare no image pull secrets, so in-project images are pulled without an explicit credential. Mirroring third-party images into that registry is the established pattern here.
The fs2-models namespace currently contains no secrets at all, so no NVIDIA registry pull secret exists on the cluster today.

The local model cache on this build host holds only unrelated media and language models. No weights for any model on this request list are cached locally. This says nothing about cluster volumes, which are separate and were inspected separately.
A model hub credential file is present on this build host, which covers the ungated artifacts; most artifacts on this list need no credential at all.

A read-only inspection of nvcr.io/nim/mit/boltz2 from this build host, using the docker credential stored in the host's docker config, returned HTTP 403 on the registry ping. This is a build-host credential result only. It was not worked around, and no alternative account, profile or region was tried.

unverified: Whether the NVIDIA registry 403 reflects an expired or unentitled credential, a missing per-organisation terms acceptance, or an entitlement scope limit was not determined, because diagnosing it further would have meant trying other credentials.

Live pull of any NVIDIA microservice from inside the cluster is unverified and is a separate question from the build-host probe. It requires creating a pull secret in the target namespace, which is a mutation this read-only task did not perform.
Free capacity was read from current GPU requests at a single point in time. It is not a reservation and says nothing about what other tenants will schedule next.
Whether the shared filesystem backing the existing cache volumes has headroom for the multi-hundred-gigabyte alignment databases was not measured; only the two existing 128Gi claims were observed.

runtime_recommendation.rationale: No NIM exists. Upstream ships its own Dockerfile with a DOWNLOAD_WEIGHTS build argument that bakes the roughly 6 GB of checkpoints into the image, which removes first-run download from the startup path and is the single most useful fast-start lever for this model. The workload is a multi-step ranked design campaign, not a request-response service.

h100_fit.vram_note: No official VRAM figure is published; the maintainers state there are no memory estimates as a function of input length. A 16 GB card fails on a large target while a 48 GB card succeeds, so 80 GB is ample headroom.
h100_fit.cpu_or_host_dependency: Host memory is the real binding constraint, not VRAM: 64 GB of RAM is required and 16 GB is reported to fail in the analysis step even at 100 designs. There is no MSA at inference at all, so no alignment sidecar, no sequence databases and no network egress during a run.
h100_fit.evidence: Per-design timings are published on an A100 and the kernel path auto-enables at compute capability 8 or above, which includes H100. An open upstream issue reports a run stalling partway through on an AMD EPYC host with an H100 while a different host completed, so H100 behaviour must be proven on the exact node type before the model is called qualified.

semantic_validator.fixture: Upstream example example/vanilla_protein/1g13prot.yaml, which ships in the repository, run under the protein-anything protocol.
success_criteria: All pipeline steps complete and the ranked output directory contains the requested budget of designs alongside the metrics CSV files.

Backbone self-consistency passes: the design and refold RMSD values sit below the pipeline's threshold, proving the designed sequence actually folds into the backbone the generator drew rather than being a hallucination.

Amino-acid composition filters pass, with no single residue exceeding roughly thirty percent. This is the explicit degenerate-output detector: poly-alanine and poly-glycine backbones can score well geometrically while not being real proteins.
Interface confidence is meaningfully above zero, showing a real binder-target interface rather than a dissociated chain.
No unresolved residues appear in the accepted designs.
semantic_validator.expected_runtime_note: A ten-design smoke run finishes in minutes with weights pre-baked. Production campaigns use ten to sixty thousand designs at roughly thirty to sixty seconds each, so a real campaign is a multi-GPU fleet workload measured in GPU-days, not a single pod.

h100_fit.vram_note: Upstream documents that memory scales roughly linearly with total residue count of target plus binder: about 550 residues on a 32 GB card and about 950 residues on an 80 GB card. For typical targets the H100 is not the binding constraint; the number of trajectories is.

h100_fit.evidence: The project wiki gives H100 timings directly: about five minutes per trajectory for a 250-residue complex and two to three hours for a 900-residue complex, with the A100 roughly four times slower. It also states that a campaign cannot be parallelised across multiple GPUs, though independent instances can run on separate cards.

semantic_validator.fixture: The upstream PD-L1 example, which ships in the repository as a single-chain target of roughly 115 residues with hotspot residue 56 and a binder length range of 65 to 150. PD-L1 is directly on-target for cancer immunotherapy and needs no external download.
success_criteria: The final design statistics file exists with at least one accepted row and at least one structure lands in the accepted directory.
The accepted structure has exactly two chains, the target coordinates are unchanged from the input, and the binder length falls inside the requested range.
The binder sequence contains no cysteine, because the default advanced settings omit it. A cysteine in the output means the constraint pipeline is broken.

At least one binder residue sits within about ten angstroms of the specified hotspot residue. A design that binds the opposite face is a silent semantic failure that every transport-level check would pass.

The PyRosetta-derived columns, in particular interface residue count and buried surface area, carry real non-zero values. This doubles as a live probe that PyRosetta initialised and is licensed, and it is the cheapest detector for the licence failure mode.
Across several seeds the accepted sequences differ from each other, ruling out mode collapse.
semantic_validator.expected_runtime_note: About five minutes per trajectory at this complex size on an H100. Easy targets need on the order of a hundred trajectories and hard targets one thousand to ten thousand, so treat a campaign as hours to weeks of single-GPU time and shard it across pods.

access_gates.action: PyRosetta is a hard unconditional import in this pipeline and there is no upstream flag to disable it. For this academic proof of concept the free academic tier applies. The exact one-time step is to obtain a Rosetta licence and a PyRosetta licence for the academic institution through the University of Washington CoMotion express licensing portal at https://els2.comotion.uw.edu/product/pyrosetta, which is free of charge for academic, non-profit and government entities. Both licences are required: PyRosetta is only licensed to entities that already hold a Rosetta licence. Licensing questions go to license@uw.edu. Until the licence is in place, run the FreeBindCraft lane instead and label its scoring fields as placeholders.
access_gates.grantor: University of Washington CoMotion, on behalf of Rosetta Commons
access_gates.credential_handling: The PyRosetta channel credentials belong in a cluster secret consumed at image build time. Never commit them, and never bake them into a pushed image layer.

blockers: Native BindCraft cannot run until the free academic PyRosetta and Rosetta licences are issued. This is a licence-acceptance step, not a technical one.

The published release tag is diverged from the default branch and points at a commit nine months older than the release it names. Pinning the tag would silently ship the wrong code, so onboarding must pin a commit SHA.
No official container image and no NIM exist. The community images on public registries are unofficial and most likely bake in PyRosetta, so they are not an acceptable supply-chain root.

runtime_recommendation.rationale: An official NVIDIA NIM for RFdiffusion exists, publishes H100 in its support matrix and its benchmark table, and removes the single largest technical risk in the open route. The open repository ships a CUDA 11.1 conda environment and a CUDA 11.6 Dockerfile, neither of which targets Hopper, so the open route requires a CUDA modernisation rebuild first. The tradeoff is capability: the NIM endpoint exposes only contigs, an input structure, hotspot residues, diffusion steps and a seed, so symmetry, guiding potentials and partial diffusion are not reachable through it. Use the NIM for the mainline binder lane and keep a rebuilt open image for the conditioning modes the NIM does not expose.
runtime_recommendation.base_image_hint: nvcr.io/nim/ipd/rfdiffusion, or a rebuilt open image on a CUDA 12 base with matching PyTorch and DGL

h100_fit.vram_note: NVIDIA documents a minimum of 12 GB of GPU memory for the NIM, so an 80 GB H100 is heavily over-provisioned for a single trajectory.
h100_fit.cpu_or_host_dependency: The NIM asks for four CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM and about 15 GB of fast local disk, and requires a recent driver.
h100_fit.evidence: H100 appears explicitly in the NIM support matrix and tops its published throughput table, so Hopper support is documented for the NIM route. The open repository is a different matter: its shipped conda environment pins CUDA 11.1 and its Dockerfile pins CUDA 11.6, neither of which covers Hopper, so the open route is untested and needs a rebuild. The target cluster was also inspected directly and runs driver 580.159.04, which meets this microservice's documented minimum of 580.

semantic_validator.fixture: The upstream binder design example, which ships in the repository: a 150-residue target chain with three named hotspot residues and a diffused binder of 70 to 100 residues, run with inference noise set to zero and a fixed seed for reproducibility.
semantic_validator.invocation: the upstream inference script in binder mode with the target PDB, hotspot residue list and a fixed number of designs
success_criteria: Every designed residue is glycine, because RFdiffusion emits backbone-only predictions. A full sequence in the output means a different model produced it.
The output has two chains, the target coordinates are unchanged from the input, and the binder length falls inside the requested range.

Consecutive backbone alpha carbons sit near 3.8 angstroms apart with no non-adjacent pair closer than about 3 angstroms. This single check catches an exploded or unfolded trajectory, which is the most common silent failure.
The binder is compact rather than extended, and its secondary-structure content is substantially more than random coil.
At least one designed residue lies within about ten angstroms of each specified hotspot residue, proving the run generated a binder rather than merely a protein.
Repeating with a fixed seed reproduces the coordinates, while different design indices produce genuinely different backbones.
If the NIM and the open route are both used, their outputs agree within the deviation NVIDIA publishes for the NIM against the open implementation.
semantic_validator.expected_runtime_note: Seconds per design at this size; the published baseline is about eleven seconds for a 100-residue protein on a much smaller GPU, so a ten-design acceptance run is a couple of minutes on an H100.

access_gates.action: None for the open route. Checkpoints download from published URLs under the same BSD instrument as the code.
access_gates.credential_handling: The checkpoint URLs are plain HTTP with opaque path segments and no published checksums. Download once, compute and record your own digests, mirror into the internal registry, and pin by digest. Pods must not fetch from the upstream host at runtime.

access_gates.action: The microservice route needs an NGC account and a personal or service API key; legacy keys are rejected. Some microservices additionally require a one-time Accept Terms click on their catalog page, once per NGC organisation. Current state, stated precisely: a read-only inspection of the registry from this build host using the host's stored docker credential returned HTTP 403 on the registry ping, and the fs2-models namespace on the cluster contains no secrets, so no pull secret exists there either. Live pull from inside the cluster is a separate question that this read-only task did not test, because it would require creating that pull secret. The exact one-time step is to obtain a valid NGC personal or service key, accept the terms for the specific microservice once per organisation, and create it as a pull secret in the target namespace. The entitlement tier also matters: NVIDIA's product terms allow these microservices without a subscription only on a workstation and explicitly exclude a server servicing multiple users, which is what this cluster is; the free developer programme separately covers research and experimentation on up to sixteen GPUs, which is the tier this academic proof of concept fits.
access_gates.credential_handling: Store the NGC key as a Kubernetes pull secret. Never commit it and never bake it into an image layer.

blockers: The open repository's shipped CUDA environments predate Hopper, so an image rebuild on a modern CUDA base is required before the open route can run on H100. This is engineering work, not a licence issue.
The upstream project has not tagged a release since 2023 and the default branch is far ahead of the last tag, so onboarding must pin a commit SHA rather than a tag.

The microservice route's free tier covers research and experimentation only. If this workload later becomes production or commercial, the NIM lane needs an NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription, whereas the open BSD route needs none. Keep the open image buildable so the lane is not trapped behind a subscription.

The microservice lane has no pull path yet: the build-host registry credential returns 403 and the target namespace holds no pull secret. Both must be resolved before the lane can start, and the in-cluster pull remains separately unverified.

runtime_recommendation.rationale: No NVIDIA NIM for AlphaFold 3 exists. DeepMind publishes no prebuilt image either, so the image is built from the repository Dockerfile. The correct shape is two workloads, not one: a CPU-only data pipeline job that performs the alignment and template search, and a single-GPU inference job that consumes its JSON output. The repository supports this split directly through flags that disable either half.
runtime_recommendation.base_image_hint: built from the upstream Dockerfile; the host needs a CUDA 12.6 capable driver

h100_fit.vram_note: An 80 GB card handles up to 5120 tokens with memory preallocation enabled. Larger inputs need the documented unified-memory setting, which spills to host memory at a speed cost. Published H100 timings run from roughly 34 seconds at 1024 tokens to about 1416 seconds at 5120 tokens.
h100_fit.cpu_or_host_dependency: The data pipeline is the dominant infrastructure cost and never touches the GPU. It needs nine genetic and structural databases totalling roughly 252 GB compressed and 630 GB unpacked, up to a terabyte of fast local disk, and at least 64 GB of RAM, with more for deep alignments.
h100_fit.evidence: The upstream documentation officially supports a single H100 80GB alongside the A100 80GB, states that numerical accuracy was verified on both, requires compute capability 8.0 or above, and publishes an H100 timing table. This is the only model on the request list with documented, benchmarked H100 support from its own upstream.

semantic_validator.fixture: Two shipped examples, run in order. First the ubiquitin monomer for a mechanical check, then the barnase-barstar complex, which is the one that matters because it exercises the interface confidence metrics an antibody-antigen user will actually consume. Both are small enough to run in minutes.
semantic_validator.invocation: the upstream inference entry point with the data pipeline disabled and a fixed model seed, pointing at the shipped example JSON
success_criteria: Output is a parseable mmCIF plus the confidence and summary confidence JSON files, with the residue and chain counts matching the input.
For ubiquitin, mean atom confidence is high and the predicted fold reproduces the known beta-grasp topology within about one angstrom of the deposited structure.
For barnase-barstar, the interface predicted TM score exceeds the upstream threshold that distinguishes a confident prediction from a failed one, and no clash flag is set.
The ranking score is not pinned near its floor. A floor value is the documented signature of a wrong-kernel or wrong-precision deployment producing heavily clashing output.
Coordinates contain no NaN values and the chain is not collapsed or extended.
semantic_validator.expected_runtime_note: Both fixtures are far below the 1024-token point, so inference is seconds. Compilation dominates the first run, which is why a shared compilation cache directory must be configured or every cold pod repays it.

access_gates.action: There is no longer a request form: DeepMind removed the approval workflow in July 2026 and the parameter file now downloads directly and unauthenticated, which this task confirmed. The legal gate did not move with the technical one. The terms restrict use to non-commercial organisations such as universities, non-profits and research institutes, which this academic proof of concept satisfies. The exact one-time step is that the academic institution's authorised representative accepts the parameters terms of use and downloads the file themselves, because the terms state the parameters may only be used if received directly from Google. Nebius may then operate that institution's own copy under the agents and contractors provision, provided the copy is not shared beyond that organisation.
access_gates.credential_handling: Never commit the parameter file and never bake it into a shared image. The terms designate the parameters as confidential information, so on a shared cluster the volume holding them must be restricted to this tenant's namespace and excluded from any shared model cache that other tenants can read.

blockers: Weights and outputs are both restricted to non-commercial use. This is acceptable for the stated academic proof of concept, but the lane cannot carry over to commercial work without a separate commercial licence, which DeepMind does not offer through this channel.
The parameters are designated confidential information, which conflicts with placing them in a shared multi-tenant model cache. Isolation must be designed in rather than retrofitted.

The alignment pipeline needs on the order of a terabyte of fast local disk and 64 GB or more of RAM. The observed GPU nodes expose only about 277 GiB of ephemeral storage and have no large local NVMe, so the databases cannot live on node-local disk. They must be placed on the shared filesystem alongside the existing model cache volumes, whose current claims are 128Gi each and would need to be sized up substantially. This is the largest infrastructure commitment of any model on the request list.

sources.established: Canonical repository, Apache-2.0 code licence, the v3.0.4 release tag and its commit, and the README statement that the parameters may only be used if received directly from Google.
Independently confirmed at retrieval by a ranged request returning HTTP 206, proving the parameter file is now directly downloadable with no form or credential.

The non-commercial restriction on parameters and output, the prohibition on publishing or sharing parameters, the sharing carve-out limited to an organisation's employees, consultants, contractors and agents, and the confidentiality designation.
Official support for a single H100 80GB, the verified numerical accuracy statement, the 5120-token ceiling, the H100 timing table and the unified-memory workaround.
Database download and unpacked sizes, the disk and RAM requirements, the CUDA 12.6 host requirement and the compute capability floor.

resolution.rationale: The operator already runs OpenFold3 and asked whether it substitutes for AlphaFold3. It resolves to one repository, and the hyphenated name is the correct one: the unhyphenated variant does not exist, and the similarly named OpenFold repository is the separate AlphaFold2 reproduction.

rejected_candidates.reason: The AlphaFold2 reproduction. A different model line, not OpenFold3.
A real but stale secondary mirror behind an access gate; it predates the current default weights. Use the ungated public object store instead.

weights.revision: of3-ob-2025-06-30-174k, roughly 2.13 GiB, confirmed reachable unauthenticated at retrieval
weights.size_note: The current default checkpoint. It requires package version 0.5.0 or newer; the older preview weights require a version below 0.5, so code and weights are version-locked and must not be mixed.

runtime_recommendation.rationale: Install the published package, pull the checkpoint from the ungated public bucket and run the documented entry point. This keeps the whole lane on a single permissive licence with no account or key in the image-pull path. An OpenFold3 NIM does exist and adds an optimised runtime, but it wraps the permissively licensed weights in an additional NVIDIA licence and a registry key dependency, which is a step backwards for an otherwise unencumbered model. As with AlphaFold3, split the work into a CPU alignment stage and a single-GPU inference stage.
runtime_recommendation.base_image_hint: the published consortium image, or a CUDA 12 base with the pinned package version

h100_fit.vram_note: Upstream requires at least 32 GB of GPU memory, and NVIDIA's own runtime documentation reports typical usage of 40 to 80 GB depending on sequence length. An 80 GB H100 sits comfortably above the minimum, so the low-memory mode should be left off because it serialises work and is markedly slower.
h100_fit.cpu_or_host_dependency: The alignment pipeline is CPU-bound and storage-hungry: roughly 330 GB of databases at minimum, rising to several terabytes if the large sequence databases are added, and upstream recommends node-local solid-state storage. The public hosted alignment service is not an option here: its operators ask that it not be queried from multiple machines, which a pod fleet inherently violates, and it would send target sequences to a third party.
h100_fit.evidence: Upstream states a CUDA 12.1 floor and a 32 GB memory minimum, and NVIDIA's runtime support matrix names H100 80GB explicitly with published per-length latencies. The model was itself trained on a large H100 fleet. Hopper support is therefore documented rather than assumed.

semantic_validator.fixture: Two shipped fixtures with upstream-calibrated thresholds. The ubiquitin query is the fast liveness check. The lysozyme-with-ligand query is the real correctness gate, because upstream publishes both a ceiling for the alignment-backed modes and a floor for the alignment-free mode.
semantic_validator.invocation: the package prediction entry point against the shipped example query, first with the alignment server disabled, then with alignments supplied
success_criteria: Output is a parseable mmCIF with per-atom confidence written into the temperature-factor column, alongside the per-atom and aggregated confidence files and a timing file.

For ubiquitin, average confidence and predicted TM score land near the values upstream records for this fixture, averaged over several diffusion samples because a single sample is not a stable measurement.
For the lysozyme fixture with alignments, backbone deviation from the reference structure falls below the tight upstream ceiling and the ligand is placed in the correct pocket.

For the same fixture without alignments, backbone deviation stays above the upstream floor. This is the decisive check: a ceiling-only test still passes when the alignment path has silently died, and a floor catches exactly that.
No clash flag is set and coordinates contain no NaN values.
semantic_validator.expected_runtime_note: Roughly ten seconds for a small target on an H100 under the optimised runtime; the plain package stack is slower. Alignment time is excluded from the reported timing and dominates end to end.

access_gates.action: None on the recommended path. The checkpoints sit in a public object store and were confirmed reachable unauthenticated at retrieval. Avoid the HuggingFace mirror, which is gated behind a questionnaire and would put a token in the pull path for no benefit.
access_gates.credential_handling: No credential needed. Fetch in an init container and cache on a shared volume.

blockers: Covalent chemistry is not expressible at inference: covalently modified residues, cross-chain covalent bonds, covalently bound ligands and polymeric ligands such as glycans are all listed by upstream as not yet supported. Point mutations and simple non-canonical residue substitutions do work. If the workload involves glycosylated antibodies or covalent conjugates, this lane cannot represent the input at all and AlphaFold3 remains necessary.

The input and output formats are not interchangeable with AlphaFold3. The schemas are semantically close but syntactically different, so a converter is needed and it must reject rather than silently drop any AlphaFold3 job that uses covalent bonds.

Upstream describes the current release as a research preview and states plainly that no reproduction has fully matched AlphaFold3 across all modalities. Reported gaps concentrate in nucleic-acid monomers, protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions.

The same storage constraint as AlphaFold3 applies to its alignment databases, which range from roughly 330 GB upwards. The observed GPU nodes have no large local NVMe, so these must sit on the shared filesystem.

sources.established: Canonical repository with the hyphenated name, Apache-2.0 licence, the v0.5.0 tag and its commit, the research-preview status, the supported-modality list and the explicitly unsupported covalent and glycan features.
Independently confirmed at retrieval: the current default checkpoint is reachable unauthenticated over HTTPS, while the withdrawn legacy checkpoint returns 404.
Published package version 0.5.0 under Apache-2.0 with release artifact checksums for immutable pinning.
That H100 80GB is an explicitly supported target with published latencies, which is what makes the H100 fit documented rather than assumed.

That the current default weights are released under Apache-2.0 together with training data and recipes, their mid-2025 structural-data cutoff, and the vendor's own benchmark comparison against AlphaFold3.

open_questions.question: Is 'mosaic' the Escalante Bio composite-objective protein design framework, whose published case studies are PD-L1 and IL7Ra minibinders?
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Proceed with the Escalante Bio framework. Evidence is strong: it is a protein design project, its case studies are cancer-immunotherapy targets, and it natively composes four other models on this request list.

open_questions.question: Which RFdiffusion generation is wanted: the original for protein-protein binders, RFdiffusion2 for enzyme active sites, or the all-atom line for small-molecule binders?
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Proceed with the original RFdiffusion. It is the one with the widely cited paper, the one NVIDIA packages as a microservice, and the correct tool for protein binder design, which is this workload's stated purpose.

open_questions.question: Protenix v2 weights are not publicly served. Should onboarding proceed on the obtainable Protenix v1 checkpoint with the later mid-2025 training cutoff, or hold the lane until v2 is released?
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Proceed on the v1 checkpoint with the later cutoff, labelled explicitly as a substitute, and re-probe the v2 object on a schedule. Holding the lane would block a secondary model on a release with no published timeline.

open_questions.question: Which Proteina-Complexa pipelines are in scope: protein-target binders, small-molecule-target binders, motif scaffolding, or all three?
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Onboard the protein-target binder pipeline first, since it matches the stated immunotherapy workload, and stage the other two checkpoints without wiring their pipelines.

open_questions.question: Does the workload need glycosylated antibodies, antibody-drug-conjugate linkers, or any other covalent conjugate modelled?
open_questions.default_if_unanswered: Assume not, and route structure prediction to OpenFold3 by default. If covalent chemistry is needed, OpenFold3 cannot express the input at all and the AlphaFold3 lane becomes required rather than optional.
